methodological_rigor.justification: The design is appropriate: a large multicenter retrospective evaluation (n=115,973) across five NHS services with a 39-month follow-up ground truth (capturing interval and next-round cancers) and a prospective noninterventional feasibility study at 12 sites (n=9,266). The primary endpoint (noninferiority of AI sensitivity/specificity vs first reader with a prespecified 5% margin) was prespecified with a documented power calculation (~25,000 women/site at ~80% power assuming 200 cancers), Holm–Bonferroni multiplicity correction, Obuchowski clustered McNemar for superiority, and bootstrap-based inference where appropriate. Weaknesses include non-blinded assessment ('Data collection and analysis were not performed blind'), replacement sampling of women lacking follow-up (acknowledged as potentially excluding underserved groups), post-hoc OP recalibration in the prospective arm, no multiplicity adjustment for the many secondary/subgroup tests, and small subgroups (e.g., mixed ethnicity n=21 positives) that limit fairness inference. Overall the methodology is solid for a translational validation study with limitations clearly acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual multicenter retrospective cohort evaluation of a diagnostic AI, complemented by a prospective observational feasibility deployment—neither is interventional nor randomized, placing it at Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: it directly addresses a population-screening question with policy implications for the NHS BSP, uses patient-relevant outcomes (CDR, interval cancer detection, invasive cancer sensitivity), examines fairness across demographic/technical subgroups, and surfaces deployment realities (distribution shift, OP recalibration, workflow digitization). Although it is not practice-changing on its own (interventional outcomes evidence still required), it meaningfully informs near-term deployment decisions and complements an interventional companion study.

reporting_quality.justification: This is primarily a diagnostic accuracy study (AI vs human readers against a 39-month ground truth), so STARD is the most relevant checklist, with elements of TRIPOD and STROBE also applicable. Reporting is thorough: trial registration (ISRCTN 60839016 and 88754382), ethics approvals, prespecified primary/secondary endpoints and noninferiority margin, flow diagram (Extended Data Fig. 1a,b), subgroup definitions, OP selection methodology, lesion annotation procedure, and explicit acknowledgment that secondary endpoints lacked multiplicity correction. Gaps include limited reporting of indeterminate results, no explicit STARD checklist, and non-blinded reads. Data availability lists Source Data for figures/tables but there is no explicit mention of a public mammogram repository or code release; the AI system is proprietary (Google), limiting external replication, hence a mid-range reproducibility score.

novelty_literature.justification: The study builds directly on the authors' prior Nature 2020 work (McKinney et al.) and recent AI-in-screening evaluations (MASAI/Lång, Lauritzen, Dembrower, Sharma), rather than introducing a first-in-class concept. Novel contributions include the use of a 39-month ground truth integrating interval and next-round cancers, breast- and lesion-level analyses with validated IoU, systematic fairness analysis across IMD/ethnicity/density/device, and an iterative prospective OP recalibration demonstrating distribution shift in a real NHS deployment. These are meaningful methodological and translational extensions rather than paradigm-shifting findings; comparable multi-vendor independent-reader validations already exist in the literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear abstract that is quantitatively grounded and faithfully reflects the results, logical methods–results–discussion flow, and informative figure captions that specify sample sizes, statistical tests, and significance notation. Terminology (OP, CDR, IMD, prevalent vs incident screens) is defined on first use and tables are self-contained. Minor issues: some long paragraphs in the Discussion that interleave findings and policy commentary could be tightened, and the heading 'AI outperformed for women's first screens and invasive cancers...' is unusually long. Overall, this reads as a publication-ready, carefully written manuscript.

key_strengths: Very large multicenter retrospective cohort (115,973 mammograms, 5 NHS services, 3 vendor platforms) with prespecified 5% noninferiority margin and documented power calculation
Rigorous 39-month ground truth incorporating interval and next-round cancers, enabling evidence of earlier detection (25% of interval cancers correctly flagged)
Appropriate statistical framework: Holm–Bonferroni multiplicity correction, Obuchowski clustered McNemar, bootstrap CIs, breast- and lesion-level analyses
Comprehensive fairness analysis across age, IMD, ethnicity, density, and device, with transparent reporting of borderline subgroups and their limitations
Prospective 12-site observational deployment that empirically demonstrates distribution shift and the need for adaptive OP recalibration—a practically important deployment insight
Translationally relevant to a national screening programme with explicit workflow, digitization, and governance considerations
key_concerns: Non-blinded assessment and no multiplicity adjustment for the large number of secondary/subgroup tests
Replacement sampling of women without follow-up may have selectively excluded underserved populations, limiting fairness conclusions
Proprietary AI model (Google v1.2) and lack of explicit code release limit external reproducibility; data-availability posture is modest
Prospective OP was recalibrated post-hoc after a 2-week review using recall-rate proxy, introducing optimism in the adjusted-OP metrics
Several subgroup analyses (mixed ethnicity, IMD decile 1) are underpowered, as the authors acknowledge
Novelty is incremental relative to McKinney 2020, MASAI, Lauritzen, and Dembrower—extensions in evaluation depth rather than paradigm shift
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, large-scale, policy-relevant validation of a mammography AI with prespecified endpoints, careful fairness and workflow analyses, and a real-world prospective deployment that exposes distribution shift—content consistent with top-tier oncology/medical AI venues, pending minor clarifications on multiplicity, OP recalibration, and reproducibility posture.
